clinicalPearls: A rare fibrosing thyroiditis presenting as a hard, fixed, painless goitre that feels woody or stony on palpation
The fibrosis extends beyond the thyroid capsule into surrounding neck structures, causing compressive symptoms such as dysphagia, stridor and hoarseness
Now recognised as part of the IgG4-related disease spectrum and may coexist with other fibrosclerotic disorders such as retroperitoneal fibrosis and sclerosing cholangitis
Most patients are initially euthyroid, but progressive gland destruction can lead to hypothyroidism and, if the parathyroids are involved, hypoparathyroidism
The fixed, infiltrative mass closely mimics anaplastic thyroid carcinoma and lymphoma, so malignancy must be excluded
Fine-needle aspiration is often non-diagnostic because of dense fibrosis, and open surgical biopsy is usually required to confirm the diagnosis
Management combines glucocorticoids, other immunosuppressive or antifibrotic therapy, and limited surgery to relieve compression rather than resection
reference.pathophysiology: Riedel thyroiditis is characterised by replacement of thyroid parenchyma with dense invasive fibrous tissue that infiltrates the capsule and adjacent cervical structures. It is increasingly regarded as a manifestation of IgG4-related disease, with a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate rich in IgG4-positive plasma cells, obliterative phlebitis and storiform fibrosis. The relentless fibrosclerotic process entraps and compresses local structures, and destruction of thyroid tissue and occasionally the parathyroid glands leads to hormonal insufficiency over time.
additionalDifferentials: Infiltrative metastatic disease of the thyroid
additionalInvestigations: Neck ultrasound and cross-sectional imaging to define the extent of infiltration and compression
Open (surgical) biopsy for definitive histology when aspiration is non-diagnostic
Serum IgG4 and assessment for associated fibrosclerotic disease
Thyroid function tests to detect hypothyroidism
Calcium and parathyroid hormone to identify hypoparathyroidism
Laryngoscopy to assess vocal-cord function where hoarseness is present
redFlags: Rapidly enlarging neck mass or stridor indicating airway compromise
Features that cannot confidently exclude anaplastic carcinoma or lymphoma
reference.prognosis: The condition is chronic but not malignant; medical therapy can arrest progression and relieve symptoms, though established fibrosis and hormonal deficiencies are usually irreversible.
pitfalls: Mistaking the fixed hard goitre for anaplastic carcinoma, or vice versa, without adequate biopsy
Relying on fine-needle aspiration, which is often uninformative in dense fibrosis
Attempting radical thyroidectomy, which is technically hazardous given the infiltration
Overlooking associated IgG4-related fibrosclerotic disease elsewhere
Missing evolving hypothyroidism or hypoparathyroidism during follow-up
references: Reference literature on IgG4-related disease and fibrosing thyroiditis
management: Glucocorticoids as first-line therapy to arrest the fibrosclerotic process and relieve compressive symptoms
Tamoxifen to suppress fibroblast proliferation, alone or with corticosteroids
Steroid-sparing immunosuppression such as rituximab or mycophenolate for refractory IgG4-related disease
Levothyroxine replacement for hypothyroidism, and calcium with active vitamin D for hypoparathyroidism if the parathyroids are involved
Limited surgical decompression such as wedge isthmusectomy to relieve tracheal or oesophageal compression, rather than radical resection
Open surgical biopsy to exclude anaplastic carcinoma and lymphoma, with surveillance for associated fibrosclerotic disease such as retroperitoneal fibrosis
Endocrinology, otolaryngology and surgical multidisciplinary follow-up
